items.text: We benchmarked 300+ NVIDIA verified skills to see how much they actually help agents on real tasks. Same task, same model, same setup. SkillEvaluator is open source if you want to test your own skills before you ship them.

items.text: Everyone sharing this token price chart as “AI demand is collapsing” is reading one line of a three-line story. So I’ve taken a shot at fixing it with the three lines that matter and make it a more objective read → Token prices (Silicon Data, via Bloomberg): round-tripped, flat over 9 months → H100 compute cost (Silicon Data, SemiAnalysis): UP 27%, capacity sold out. → Token volume (OpenRouter): UP ~7x, and that’s the paid sliver of a market Google alone runs at more than 3.2 quadrillion tokens/month Flat prices + rising input costs + exploding volume = deflation by engineering, not weak demand. Also, new architectures Blackwell, MI, Rubin etc all offer greater token efficiency versus H100. Margin growth slows/stalls but should improve as capacity is brought online. The falling line isn’t the bust. It’s the buildout working. Second image is the original chart. Attribution in the footnotes.

items.text: We just released TensorRT Model Connect in Public Preview. You can take a supported @huggingface model to end-to-end TensorRT inference in just two commands. No intermediate ONNX export, and the resulting bundle can run through native C++ APIs. We also built the entire project with @OpenAIDevs Codex agents, with humans directing and reviewing the work. That includes model implementations, performance tuning, tests, integrations, and docs. It’s open source, so go try it out, dig into the implementations, or contribute support for a new model: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-Model-Connect
